quests.title: Lamentation of the Dead Christ
quests.completionMessage: Lamentation of the Dead Christ was painted by Giotto di Bondone between 1304-06 The fragmentary New Testament scenes on the wall of the Upper Church include Christ among the Doctors, the Baptism of Christ, the Lamentation and the Resurrection. The work which is considered to be Giotto"s greatest is in the city of Padua, Italy, about 25 miles from venice. He was commissioned to decorate the Arena Chapel.... Thirty-four frescoes are painted in the three divisions. The lower division is made up of scenes from the Passion of Christ. Giotto uses only what is needed to tell the story and express the feelings involved/ We can best gauge the extent of this revolution if we compare one of Giotto"s frescoes from Padua, with a similar theme in the thirteenth-century miniature. The subject is the mourning over the dead body of Christ, with the Virgin embracing her Son for the last time.

quests.title: Additional Info Lamentation of the Dead Christ
quests.completionMessage: In the miniature the artist was not interested in representing the scene as it might have happened. He varied the size of the figures so as to fit them well into the page, and if we try to imagine the space between the figures in the foreground and St John in the background - with Christ and the Virgin in between - we realize how everything is squeezed together, and how little the artist cared about space. It is the same indifference to the real place where the scene is happening which led Nicola Pisano to represent different episodes within one frame. Giotto"s method is completely different. Painting, for him, is more than a substitute for the written word. We seem to witness the real event as if it were enacted on a stage. Compare the conventional gesture of the mourning St John in the miniature with the passionate movement of St John in Giotto"s painting as he bends forward, his arms extended sideways. If we try here to imagine the distance between the cowering figures in the foreground and St John, we immediately feel that there is air and space between them, and that they can all move. These figures in the foreground show how entirely new Giotto"s art was in every respect. We remember that early Christian art had reverted to the old Oriental idea that to tell a story clearly every figure had to be shown completely, almost as was done in Egyptian art. Giotto abandoned these ideas. He did not need such simple devices. He shows us so convincingly how each figure reflects the grief of the tragic scene that we sense the same grief in the cowering figures whose faces are hidden from us.

quests.title: Artist
quests.completionMessage: Giotto di Bondone (1267-1337).  was an Italian painter and architect. He is generally considered the first in a line of great artists who contributed to and developed the Italian Renaissance.Giotto was born in poverty in the countryside near Florence, the son of Bondone, a peasant, and was himself a shepherd.  Cimabue saw him drawing a sheep, so natural and so perfect that he immediately asked his father if he could bring Giotto with him to let him study art, and Giotto"s career would have started in Cimabue"s bottega. Another story by Vasari has Giotto as an apprentice painting a fly on the nose of a figure so life like Cimabue made numerous attempts to brush the fly away. His art was extremely innovative, and is commonly considered as a precursor of that evolution which was to lead, shortly after, to the explosion of the Italian Rinascimento. He stands as the key link between the Byzantine art of the late middle ages, and the more realistic and humanistic art which flowered in the Renaissance. The flat, symbolic figures grouped in decorative space gave way to the modeled, individualized figures interacting in perspectival space. He managed to adopt the visual language of the sculptors — by lending his figures volume and weight. Compare his Madonna to that of his teacher Cimabue, and you see why his contemporaries considered Giotto"s paintings miracles of naturalism.

quests.title: Madonna in Glory
quests.completionMessage: Madonna in Glory was painted by Giotto di Bondone in 1295 Images of Mary enthroned as the heavenly mother of Christ was another popular icon. She is always the center of the composition, and hierarchic scale also makes sure that she is the focus of attention. The gold background reinforces her divine status, as do the surrounding angels. There are strong similarities between these two images, given the conventions that dictated her representation, but if you look carefully, you will note that Giotto begins to define Mary in more three-dimensional terms. We will see this tendency develop further as we move into the Renaissance period.

quests.title: Madonna & Child
quests.completionMessage: Madonna & Child was painted by Giovanni Bellini in 1480 This beautiful picture, painted in the late 1480s, is a work of Giovanni Bellini"s maturity. Unusually, the cloth of honor behind the figures is off center, revealing a distant landscape that in its light and atmosphere looks forward to the works of Giorgione and Titian. The fine Venetian frame dates from the early sixteenth century.

quests.title: Artist
quests.completionMessage: Giovanni Bellini (1430-1516) Giovanni Bellini was initially taught by his father Jacopo Bellini whose icon-like method and manner influenced his early work. When Giovanni’s sister Nicosia married Andrea Mantegna in 1453, close relations between Venice and Padua were established, and Giovanni began to explore the physical and special representation of the Early Renaissance. Under Mantegna’s influence his style assumed temporarily a certain calligraphic precision. More than 200 of his works survived till our days, among them 50 images of Madonna with Infant.

quests.title: Paris A Rainy Day
quests.completionMessage: Paris A Rainy Day was painted by Gustave Caillebotte in 1877 The artist’s family owned property in the busy neighborhood depicted here, which was populated by wealthy Parisians and workers of various sorts. In the foreground, a man and woman wearing fashionable clothes stroll down the sidewalk. Behind them stand the uniformly designed buildings that were added to Paris during the renovations overseen by French administrator Baron Haussmann.The highly crafted surface, monumental size, geometric order, and elaborate perspective of Paris Street; Rainy Day (the artist used a gaslight to separate the foreground from the middle and distant views) are more academic than Impressionist in character. Caillebotte clearly intended these elements to underscore the power of painting to capture the momentary quality of everyday life. In this cropped composition, it is easy to imagine that in just a moment, everyone in the painting will have moved and nothing will be the same

quests.title: Artist
quests.completionMessage: Gustave Caillebotte (1848-1894) Caillebotte inherited a sizable fortune after his father"s death in 1874, which funded his patronage of the arts. Also, in 1874 he attended the École des Beaux-Arts where he met impressionist painters Edgar Degas, Claude Monet, and Pierre Auguste Renoir.His painting style appears to belong to the school of realism, although he helped organize the first impressionist exhibition and enthusiastically collected of impressionist works.Caillebotte"s painting themes were catholic. For example, he painted portraits and interior scenes, urban life, still lifes, and landscapes and seascapes. He often chose an overhead vantage point for his compositions and depicted elegantly dressed figures strolling with the expressionless look of sleep walkers (Boulevard Vu d"en Haut. 1880.). His metropolitan scenes led editor Anne Distel to title a book about him, Gustave Caillebotte: Urban Impressionist.For many years, Caillebotte"s reputation as a painter was superseded by his reputation as a supporter of the arts. However, 70 years after his death, art historians began reevaluating his artistic contributions.Just two years before he died, he married Emilie Schlauch.Gustave Caillebotte died in 1894 of pulmonary congestion .  In his will, Caillebotte donated his entire collection to the French government and 40 of his works hang in the Musee d"Orsay.

quests.title: La Belle Irlandaise
quests.completionMessage: La Belle Irlandaise was painted by Gustave Courbet in 1866 This "beautiful Irishwoman" is Johanna Hiffernan, mistress of the artist James McNeill Whistler (1834–1903), and later, of Courbet. In 1865, Whistler, Monet, and Courbet painted together at the French seaside resort of Trouville, where Jo posed for Courbet. This is one of four versions of the painting; it is both a portrait and the artist"s personal interpretation of the traditional theme of Vanity.

quests.title: Artist
quests.completionMessage: Gustave Courbet-1819-77). The painter Courbet started and dominated the French movement toward realism. Art critics and the public were accustomed to pretty pictures that made life look better than it was. Courbet, against much opposition, truthfully portrayed ordinary places and people. Gustave Courbet was born on June 10, 1819, to a prosperous farming family in Ornans, France. He went to Paris in 1841, supposedly to study law, but he soon decided to study painting and learned by copying the pictures of master artists. In 1844 his self-portrait, Courbet with a Black Dog, was accepted by the Salon, an annual public exhibition of art sponsored by the influential Royal Academy. In 1848 a political revolution in France foreshadowed a revolution in art, as people in the arts became more open to new ideas. Courbet"s early work was exhibited successfully in 1849. In 1855 he completed a huge canvas, The Artist"s Studio, and, when it was refused for an important exhibition, Courbet boldly displayed his work himself near the exhibition hall.

quests.title: Artist
quests.completionMessage: Gustave Dore (1832-1883) He was born in Strasbourg and published his first illustrated story at 15. He became a book illustrator in Paris, and his commissions included work by Rabelais, Balzac, and Dante. In 1853 he was asked to illustrate the works of Lord Byron. This was followed by other work for British publishers, including a new illustrated English Bible. He also illustrated an oversized edition of E. A. Poe"s The Raven.Doré"s English Bible (1865) was a great success, and in 1867 he had a major exhibition of his work in London. This led to the foundation of the Doré Gallery in New Bond Street.In 1869, Blanchard Jerrold, the son of Douglas William Jerrold, suggested that they work together to produce a comprehensive portrait of London. Jerrold had got the idea from The Microcosm of London produced by Rudolph Ackermann, William Pyne, and Thomas Rowlandson in 1808.Gustave Doré also illustrated several fairy tales.. Doré continued to illustrate books until his death in Paris in 1883. He is buried in the city"s Père Lachaise Cemetery.

quests.completionMessage: Gustave Moreau (1826-1898) Moreau"s main focus was the illustration of Christian and mythological figures. As a painter of literary ideas rather than visual images, his images appealed to the imagination of some Symbolist writers and artists, who saw him as the precursor to their movement.He became professor at École des Beaux-Arts of Paris in 1891 and counted among his many students the fauvist painters Henri Matisse and Georges Rouault  He is buried in Paris at the Cimetière de Montmartre.The "Musée Gustave Moreau" at 14, rue de la Rochefoucauld in Paris is one of the most extravagant in the city. The museum is in his former workshop, and opened to the public in 1903

quests.title: Judith I
quests.completionMessage: Judith I was painted by Gustav Klimt in 1901 was considered the incarnation of the femme fatale. In the Old Testament, Judith is a devout widow who captivated with her beauty the attention of the Assyrian leader who was a deadly menace to her people. At the meal in her honor he drank so much wine that he fell asleep before he could touch her. In his sleep, Judith killed him with his own sword, escaped with the help of a maid and helped the Israelites defeat the Assyrians who were now without a leader. In the Christian tradition, Judith was the allegory of the victory of chastity over vice and of humility over arrogance. At the beginning of the Reformation and Counter-Reformation, she became the symbol of freedom, justice and just beliefs. In 1840, German poet Friedrich Hebbel reinterpreted the myth: Judith was still a widow, but a virgin because her husband had been impotent. Sexually frustrated, she was attracted by the Assyrian Holofernes and killed him as a personal vengence. In Sigmund Freud"s interpretation of 1917, Judith agreed with Hebbel: Judith killed the Assyrian because he had taken her virginity.

quests.title: Additional Info Judith I
quests.completionMessage: Cutting of his head was, according to Freud, a symbol for Holofernes" castration. According to Daniela Hammer - the information on Judith comes from her catalogue essay - Klimt"s portrait falls in the same category: She is a strong and independent woman who challenges male dominance, the femme fatale symbolizes an eternal truth. Despite the fact that Klimt wrote "Judith und Holofernes" on the portrait"s frame, in 1905, at a Berlin exhibition, the painting was considered to represent Salome. To mix up such contrary figures like Judith and Salome has a long tradition in art history which dates back to the 16th century. Salome was responsible for the killing of St. John the Baptist. For the artists of the turn of the century, Salome and not Judith was the incarnation of the femme fatale. Gustave Moreau"s painting inspired Oscar Wilde to his dramatic ballad of 1893. Judith"s "subversive ambivalence" of the Renaissance in Klimt"s painting largely gave way to a sensual and erotic optic: Judith is an icon of femininity. Whatever interpretation you prefer, one fact remains: Judith I of 1901 is not only one of Gustav Klimt"s best paintings, it is one of the outstanding female portraits in art history

quests.title: Artist
quests.completionMessage: Gustav Klimt (1862-1918) Gustav Klimt was born in Baumgarten, near Vienna, Austria. He was educated at the Vienna Kunstgewerbe Art School in the years 1879-1883. Klimt was also an honorary member of the Universities of Munich and Vienna.His major works include paintings, murals, sketches and other art objects, many of which are on display in the Vienna Secession gallery.Klimt was one of the founding members of the so-called Wiener Sezession (Vienna Secession) and of the periodical "Ver Sacrum". His work is distinguished by an elegant use of gold backgrounds and mosaic patterns. This can be seen in Judith I (1901, visible at right) and in The Kiss (1907). Art historians have noted a highly eclectic range of influences contributing to Klimt"s distinct style, including Egyptian, Minoan, Classical Greek, and Byzantine inspirations. Klimt was also inspired by engravings of Albrecht Dürer, late medieval European painting, and Japanese woodcuts ("Ukiyo-e").Klimt left the Sezession movement in 1908. He died in Vienna of pneumonia and was interred at the Hietzing Cemetery, Vienna.

quests.title: Mada Primavesi
quests.completionMessage: Mada Primavesi was painted by Gustav Klimt 1912. Mäda Primavesi was the daughter of the banker and industrialist Otto Primavesi, one of the financial backers of the Wiener Werkstätte, and the actress Eugenia Primavesi (née Butschek), whom Klimt painted in 1913. Young Mäda"s portrait was executed in 1912. A series of preliminary pencil sketches, now in public and private collections, show that as the composition evolved the artist experimented with alternative poses and background motifs. Ultimately, he selected an open, painterly treatment that contrasts with the highly stylized designs adapted for backgrounds of his fin-de-siécle portraits. The lighthearted, decorative motifs seem particularly appropriate to the nine-year-old sitter

quests.title: The Italian Women
quests.completionMessage: The Italian Women was painted by Henri Mattisse in 1916Henri Matisse often painted the same subject in versions that range from relatively realistic to more abstract or schematic. At times the transition from realism to abstraction could be enacted in a single canvas, as is the case with The Italian Woman, the first of many portraits Matisse painted of a professional Italian model named Laurette. The purposefully visible pentimenti and labored convergence of lines bear witness to his perpetual struggle “to reach that state of condensation of sensations which constitutes a picture.” Matisse was not interested in capturing momentary impressions; he strove to create an enduring conception. From the earlier state of the portrait, which depicts a heavier woman, Matisse pared down Laurette’s image, in the process making her less corporeal and more ethereal. Using the conventions of religious painting—a frontal pose, introspective countenance, and flat back-ground devoid of any indication of location—he created an icon of Woman. The emphatic eyes and brow, elongated nose, and pursed lips of her schematic face resemble an African mask, implying that Matisse, like so many Modern artists, equated the idea of Woman with the foreign, exotic, and “primitive”; he continued in this vein, posing the same model with a turban and a mantilla. The spatial ambiguity of this portrait—the way the arms appear flat while the background overtakes a shoulder, for example—reveals Matisse’s relationship to Paul Cézanne via the bolder experiments of Cubism [more]. In a 1913 portrait of his wife, Matisse had played with the distinctions between volume and plane by including a flattened scarf that wraps around her arm. This treatment anticipates the shawl-like background of The Italian Woman. These paintings recall Cézanne’s series of portraits of Madame Cézanne (one of which was owned by Matisse) both formally and iconographically, although Matisse’s images are more radically schema-tized and distilled. The austerity of color and severe reduction of The Italian Woman is characteristic of Matisse’s work from 1914 to 1918. The art historian Pierre Schneider has suggested that these elements embody the artist’s response to the devastation of World War I.

quests.title: Artist
quests.completionMessage: Henri Matisse(1869-1954)Henri Matisse was born on December 31, 1869 in Le Cateau Cambresis, France. When he was young he had no interest in art. His parents owned a store. They expected him to become a lawyer or take over the store when he was older.When Henri was 29 he married Amèlie Parayre. He had 3 children. When his wife wasn"t busy with the children she would pose for his paintings At one time during his life he was so poor he ate only rice and he tried not to eat the fruit he bought to paint. This is because he was a painter who used lots of bright colors and patterns which his critics did not like at all.  They started calling him the KING OF THE WILD BEASTS (in French, his art style is called Fauvism)! He liked to do paintings with people because it made it easy for him to express his feelings about life. He especially liked to paint women, because he said they held the answer to the mystery of life. Because Matisse had cancer, he became confined to a wheelchair. From his wheelchair, he completed one of his most famous works, painting the inside of the Chapelle du Rosaire. Matisse died in 1954.

quests.title: At The Moulin Rogue
quests.completionMessage: At the Moulin Rogue was painted by Henri Toulouse-Lautrec in 1892 Because of childhood injuries that left his legs crippled, Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec often felt left out of the aristocratic world into which he had been born and lived at times on the margins of society. He frequented the Moulin Rouge, a famous Parisian nightclub named for the red windmill on its roof; here, he depicted many of his friends and favorite entertainers.In the background, La Goulue, the Moulin Rouge’s reigning dance star, adjusts her red hair while the dwarfish Toulouse-Lautrec and his tall cousin, Gabriel Tapié de Céléyran, walk toward the left. The glum assembly of characters seated around the table includes writer Edouard Dujardin, entertainer La Macarona, photographer Paul Sescau, winemaker Maurice Guibert, and another redhead, perhaps entertainer Jane Avril. The woman with the green face illuminated with artificial light is May Milton, another popular dancer of the day. Toulouse-Lautrec’s Post-Impressionist style is a highly personal combination of the Impressionists’ interest in contemporary subject matter and his own expressionistic color and line. The eerie green light of the interior evokes an unhealthy atmosphere. The artist then added to the visual drama by utilizing different lines, such as the curving silhouette of La Goulue fixing her hair, the collar of Avril’s coat, and the outline of Milton’s sleeve. These lines contrast with the strong diagonals of the banister and the floorboards, which rush forward toward the viewer, enhancing the lively mood of the decidedly worldly setting

quests.title: Artist
quests.completionMessage: Henri Toulouse-Lautrec-(1864-1901) Born on Nov. 24, 1864, in Albi, France. He was an aristocrat, the son and heir of Comte Alphonse-Charles de Toulouse and last in line of a family that dated back a thousand years. Henri"s father was rich, handsome, and eccentric. His mother was overly devoted to her only living child. Henri was weak and often sick. By the time he was 10 he had begun to draw and paint. At 12 young Toulouse-Lautrec broke his left leg and at 14 his right leg. The bones failed to heal properly, and his legs stopped growing. He reached young adulthood with a body trunk of normal size but with abnormally short legs. He was only 4 1/2 feet tall. Deprived of the kind of life that a normal body would have permitted, Toulouse-Lautrec lived wholly for his art. He stayed in the Montmartre section of Paris, the center of the cabaret entertainment and bohemian life that he loved to paint. He would sit at a crowded nightclub table, laughing and drinking, and at the same time he would make swift sketches. The next morning in his studio he would expand the sketches into bright-colored paintings. Toulouse-Lautrec began to drink heavily. In the 1890s the drinking started to affect his health. He was confined to a sanatorium and to his mother"s care at home, but he could not stay away from alcohol. Toulouse-Lautrec died on Sept. 9, 1901, at the family chateau of Malrome.

quests.title: Hell
quests.completionMessage: Hell was painted by Hieronymus Bosch in the 1500s

quests.title: Artist
quests.completionMessage: Hieronymus Bosch (1450-1516) Bosch lived and worked in ‘s-Hertogenbosch, the place from which he takes his name, a  fairly quiet Dutch city. He had 2 brothers and a sister; brother Goossen was also a painter. His training as a painter Bosch, most probably, received in the family. Some time between 1479 and 1481 Bosch married Aleyt Goyaerts van den Meervenne, evidently some years his senior. She came from a good family and had considerable wealth of her own.  In 1486-87, Bosch’s name appears for the first time in the membership lists of the Brotherhood of Our Lady, with which he was closely associated for the rest of his life. This brotherhood was one of the many groups devoted to the worship of the Virgin, which flourished in the late Middle Ages. Most of Bosch’s family belonged to the Brotherhood, and were employed by them in various tasks. There is no documentary evidence that Bosch ever left his home town. One final entry in the accounts of the Brotherhood of Our Lady records Bosch’s death in 1516.

quests.title: The Drinkers
quests.completionMessage: The Drinkers was painted by Honore Daumier in 1860 This painting, which was first exhibited in Paris in 1861, bears some resemblance to an illustration by Gavarni that was published twenty years earlier. The escape that alcohol offered to the poor is typical of the social themes Daumier explored throughout his career. The first owner of this work was the landscape painter Charles Daubigny.

quests.title: Artist
quests.completionMessage:
Honore Daumier- (1808-1879)
French caricaturist, painter and sculptor. He began work as a graphic artist, having learnt lithography techniques in 1830, and been employed on Charivari and La Caricature (1830-35) until the latter"s suppression by the government. He was imprisoned in 1832 for his anti-monarchical satire of Louis Philippe as Gargantua. After 1848, he produced watercolours which continued this vein, parodying the Courts of Justice, and depicting the existence of the poorHe became blind in old age, and was rescued from poverty by Corot, who was one of his many artistic admirers. Degas collected his work which was appreciated by Delacroix and Baudelaire as well as, perhaps not surprisingly, Balzac. He was also greatly admired by the 20th century Expressionists, who applauded both his radical stance and the freedom with which he used materials."

quests.title: Artist
quests.completionMessage: Ilya Repin (1844-1930)   Ilya Efimovich Repin was born in a small Ukrainian town of Tchuguev in the family of a military settler. As a boy he was trained as an icon painter. At the age of 19 he entered the St. Petersburg Academy of Arts. In 1873, Repin went abroad. For some months he had been traveling in Italy and then settled and worked in Paris up to 1876. It was in Paris that he witnessed the first exhibition of the Impressionists, but, judging by the works created then and by his letters home, he didn"t become the ardent follower of this new Paris school of painting, though he didn"t share the opinion of some of his country-men who saw a dangerous departure from “the truth of life” in Impressionism.  The last quarter of the 19th century is the best period in Repin’s work, though his creative activity continued in the 20th century (the artist died in 1930), he did not paint any masterpieces then. After the bolsheviks’ revolution in 1917 he lived and worked in his estate Penates in Finland. There is a Repin museum. The museum visitors have the opportunity of gaining a detailed knowledge of the artist"s life and work.

quests.completionMessage: View of the Cost Near St Petersburg was painted by Ivan Aivazovsky in 1835

quests.title: Artist
quests.completionMessage: Ivan Aivazovsky (1817-1900) Ivan Konstantinovich Aivazovsky was born in the family of a merchant of Armenian origin in the town of Feodosia, Crimea.  His parents were under strained circumstances and he spent his childhood in poverty. With the help of people who had noticed the talented youth, he entered the Simpheropol gymnasium, and then the St. Petersburg Academy of Arts, where he took the landscape painting course and was especially interested in marine landscapes.  In the course of his work, Aivazovsky evolved his own method of depicting the motion of the sea – from memory, without preliminary sketches, limiting himself to rough pencil outlines. Aivazovsky’s phenomenal memory and romantic imagination allowed him to do all this with incomparable brilliance. The development of this new method reflected the spirit of the age, when the ever-increasing romantic tendencies put an artist"s imagination to the front.

quests.title: Napolean
quests.completionMessage: Napolean was painted by Jacques-Louis David In 1797 he met Napoleon and was granted a single portrait sitting, during which David did not manage to paint much, but was absolutely captivated by Napoleon"s personality

quests.title: Artist
quests.completionMessage: Jacques-Louis David (1748-1825) David was born into the family of a wealthy Parisian merchant.  When the boy was about 10 years old his father, Louis-Maurice, died after a pistol duel. David"s two uncles, François Buron (1731-1818) and Jacques- François Desmaisons (c.1720-89) who were both architects and building contractors, took care of the boy"s upbringing. First he was educated at a boarding school and the Collège des Quatre Nations in Paris. When he decided on the career of an artist his uncles helped him to become a student of Joseph-Marie Vien (1716-1809), a professor at the Academy who had a reputation as a good teacher. In 1766-1774 David studied at the Royal Academy of Painting and Sculpture, in Vein"s class. The goal of practically every Academy student was to win the premier student prize: the Grand Prix, or Prix de Rome. David took part in the competition every year starting from 1770, until at last in 1774 he finally won it with Antiochus and Stratonice.  David enthusiastically greeted the French Revolution and from 1789 he actively participated in political life. In 1791 he was elected a deputy of the Convention from Paris. He voted for the death of Louis XVI in 1793 and supported Robespierre’s and the left radicals’ regime

quests.title: Oath of the Horati
quests.completionMessage: Oath of the Horati was painted by Jacques-Louis David in 1784 The three brothers, the Horatii, chosen by Rome to defy the champions of the town of Alba called the Curiaces, are taking an oath that they will win or die and are receiving swords from their father. Like Corneille in his tragedy "Horace", David contrasts the stoic resolution of the warriors, underlined by strict geometry and strident colour, with the gentle line of the women which expresses their suffering. Painted in 1784 and shown in Paris the following year, this painting earned David a European reputation as uncontested leader of the Neoclassical movement

quests.title: Artist
quests.completionMessage: James McNeill Whistler (1834-1903) James McNeill Whistler was born in Lowell, Massachusetts, USA.  He spent five years of his childhood (1843-1848) in St. Petersburg, Russia, where his father, George Washington Whistler (1800-1849), a railroad engineer, was employed in the building of the St. Petersburg-Moscow railroad. The artist’s mother, Anna Matilda McNeill, was a devout Christian, whom he admired all his life. In his early manhood he exchanged his middle name ‘Abbott’ for her maiden name ‘McNeill’.  In St. Petersburg young James received his first art lessons in the Imperial Academy of Fine Arts and also learnt French. In 1849, Major Whistler died and his wife decided to bring her family to their homeland, setting at Pomfret, Connecticut, where James attended the local school until, in 1851, he entered West Point, the famous military academy. Never becoming a military man, Whistler remembered the three years spent at the academy with affection.  Among all subjects Whistler succeeded only in drawing, special difficulties were caused by chemistry, which at last became the reason of his ejection from the academy. ‘Had silicon been a gas,’ He later declared, ’I would have been a general-major’.

quests.title: Artist
quests.completionMessage:
Jan
 van Eyck is considered to be a founder of the Early Renaissance style in the Northern Renaissance.  it is believed that he was born in early 1390s in the eastern province of the Netherlands Limburg. He probably was taught the art by his brother Hubert van Eyck, but after the death of Hubert, his younger brother finished it alone.  Until 1425 Jan van Eyck served at the court of Duke Johann of Bavaria in Hague, painting and restoring pictures. Since 1425 he served at the court of Philip the Good of Burgundy, where he was greatly valued not only as an artist, but he also was entrusted by Duke with various diplomatic missions. Since 1430 van Eyck lived and worked in Bruges as painter to the court and city. It was believed, that Jan van Eyck invented painting with oils, maybe it is not true, but his technique in painting with oils is exceptional. His paint is so transparent that his works have a unique, almost luminous sheen 1395-1491

quests.title: Portrait of Cardinal Nicola Albergati
quests.completionMessage: Portrait of Cardinal Nicola Albergati was painted by Jan van Eyck in 1432 Jan van Eyck is considered one of the founders and leading masters of Early Netherlandish panel painting. His portrait shows Cardinal Niccolò Albergati, head of the Carthusian Order, who travelled on a pontifical mission to the courts of England, France and Burgundy for peace negotiations to end the Hundred Years War between England and France. Jan van Eyck, court painter to Duke Philip the Good of Burgundy, made a silverpoint sketch (today in Dresden) in one portrait sitting as a preparatory drawing for this painting. Despite the realistic, carefully observed traces of age in the old mans face, the portrait radiates dignified repose.

quests.title: Virgin of the Chancellor Rolin
quests.completionMessage: Virgin of the Chancellor Rolin was painted by Jan van Eyck between 1434-36 The Chancellor of Burgundy, Nicolas Rolin (1376/1462) commissioned this picture of himself kneeling in prayer before the Madonna, with Jesus blessing him. He was a high dignitary in the court of Philippe the Good (one of whose good deeds was to have commissioned Van der Weyden to paint the altar-piece of the Last Judgement for the Beaune hospice). The urban landscape in the background does not, despite its apparent precision, depict a real town but is rather a juxtaposition of several existing sites. All the minutely rendered detail has a precise religious significance. Van Eyck conferred an intense spiritual value upon the infinitely small, with a perfect, almost alchemical mastery of his technique.

quests.title: Artist
quests.completionMessage: Joseph Mallord William Turner  1775-1851- Turner was only fourteen years old when he was admitted to the Royal Academy Schools. He started his career by painting watercolours and producing mezzotints under the strong influence of John Robert Cozen"s work. Then, in 1796, he launched into oil painting, working in the neoclassical manner of Richard Wilson and Nicolas Poussin, with results that found wide acclaim.  He was elected an Associate in 1799 and in 1802 a full member of the Royal Academy. Turner was one of the most prolific painters of his time. He traveled extensively in England, Scotland and Ireland, and also on the Continent (France, Belgium, Holland, Germany, Italy). In 1802, he visited Paris for the first time, where he studied the Old Masters in the Louvre, above all Dutch seascapes and Claude Lorrain"s compositions, which lastingly influenced him. Turner"s first private showing, at his own house, took place in 1804. During this period, thanks to the increasing concentration on the atmospheric effects of light, his original style began to evolve, a process that culminated during trips to Italy between 1819 and 1829.

quests.title: The Corination of the Virgin
quests.completionMessage: The Corination of the Virgin was painted by Fra Angelico between1434-35.A masterpiece of serene piety and harmonious colouring, the Coronation of the Virgin was painted for the church of the Dominican convent of Fiesole. The predella depicts the Entombment of Christ and six episodes from the life of St. Dominic who founded the order to which the painter belonged. Clever use of perspective and a skilful placing of figures in space demonstrate that despite his Medieval sensibility Fra Angelico was one of the first to make use of the architectonic discoveries of Brunelleschi and Masaccio which ushered in the Florentine Renaissance.

quests.title: Artist
quests.completionMessage: Fra Angelico (1387-1455) Fra Angelico was a Dominican, and a mendicant, so, not being part of a closed order, he was free to meet and talk to others in the city.  In 1420-1422, he entered the convent of San Domenico in Fiesole with his brother Benedetto. It was here that he produced his first works  Fra Angelico not only gained recognition as a painter, but must have commanded respect in his convent because he was appointed Vicario for the first time in Fiesole from 1432/33, a post he was to hold frequently in later years. In the 1430’s the painter worked in Florentine churches.

quests.title: The Clothed Maja
quests.completionMessage: The Clothed Maja was painted between 1800-03 is first recorded in Godoy’s collection, and the importance of his position suggests the possibility that they were painted for him. Both the origin of the Majas and the identity of the model are still a mystery. Goya was summoned by the Inquisition in 1815 to explain when and for whom they had been executed, but his explanation has never been brought to light.

quests.title: Artist
quests.completionMessage: Francisco Goya- (1746-1828) Goya was born in a very poor village called Fuendetodos, near Saragossa, in Aragon.  Goya’s father was a gilder in Saragossa and it was there that Goya spent his childhood and adolescence. He began his artistic studies at the age of 13 with a local artist, José Lusán, who had trained in Naples and who taught Goya to draw, to copy engravings and to paint in oils. In 1763 and 1766, he competed unsuccessfully for a scholarship of the Royal Academy of San Fernando in Madrid, probably working in the studio of the Court Painter Francisco Bayeu, who was also from Saragossa. To continue his studies he went to Rome at his own expense. In April of 1771 he participated in a competition held by the Academy of Parma introducing himself as a pupil of Francisco Bayeu During a visit to Andalusia towards the end of 1792, Goya was struck down by a long and serious illness of which the effect, as he wrote even a year later, made him, ‘At times rage with so ill a humor that he could not tolerate himself’. The nature of the illness is not known for certain but it caused temporary paralysis and partial blindness and left him permanently deaf, so that henceforth he could only communicate by writing and sign language

quests.title: Aqualaz upgrade: Part 1 of 3
quests.description: "So, you came to upgrade your Aqualaz? Well, I can help you with that, if you help me get back at that evil scum Justin. First I need you to go nearby and get me 5 Wispion meats."
quests.completionMessage: "Great, you got them, I have a few more things I need you to do before I can upgrade your gun though. Justin is going to pay for his evildoings."

quests.title: Aqualaz upgrade: Part 2 of 3
quests.description: "Alright, for this next one, you"re going to have to break out your smithing skills, I need a (AP)Bloodhasten. If you can"t make it, buy it from someone, I don"t care, I just need it so I can scare the pants off of Justin."
quests.completionMessage: "Oh, great, thank you. There"s just one problem, while you were away, me and Justin made up, so I have no need for this anymore. But I do need something from you before I can upgrade your weapon." [More]

quests.title: Aqualaz upgrade: referral
quests.description: "Ok, what I need is one (AP)Aqualaz, an (AP)Amberlaz and one Elite Shockion Head."
quests.completionMessage: "Now I"m ready to pimp your weapon. You"ll be able to expect up to a 20 hit point enhancement. If you don"t think that is enough, then I suggest you head right over to my mentor Strigos on Amphibious Island. He uses an, albeit riskier, method than I. But his results can sometimes be fascinating. Here"s a pass to talk to him. Or, you can play it safe and let me take care of your upgrade."
quests.hint: Its either me or Strigos, Your choice.

quests.title: Aqualaz upgrade: Part 3 of 3
quests.description: "Ok, what I need is one (AP)Aqualaz, an (AP)Amberlaz and one Elite Shockion Head."
quests.completionMessage: "Good, Strigos is a kook anyway! Now... I just extract the eyes from this head...I use some magic to transfer the power of the Amberlaz to the Aqualaz, and seal and enhance the power with this extract I have made from the eyes...Here you go! An upgraded Aqualaz." [More]

quests.title: Aqualaz upgrade: Complete
quests.description: "You can expect this Aqualaz to do up to 20 more damage than a normal Aqualaz. If you wanted more than that, you should have listened to me when I told you to see my mentor Strigos on Amphibious Island."

Hop on the final pad to go to your instructor."

quests.title: Introduction
quests.completionMessage: Welcome to Racelands!  The first of all the courses is "Green Course".  To complete this course, you must drive through each green ring in succession before the timer runs out.  Your engine will be upgraded automatically upon completion. [More]

quests.title: Green Course
quests.description: Drive through the first green ring to begin the course. [Go]
quests.completionMessage: Your next course is "Yellow Course".  To complete this course, you must drive through each yellow ring in succession before the timer runs out.  Your tires will be upgraded upon completion. [More]

quests.title: Yellow Course
quests.description: Drive through the first yellow ring to begin the course. Be careful of the U-turn.  As usual, drive though the rings and keep going on to the next.  [Go]
quests.completionMessage: You"re ready for "Red Course".  The most dangerous of all the courses.  To complete "Red Course", you must drive through each red ring in succession before the timer runs out.  Your vehicle will be enhanced upon completion. [More]

quests.title: Red Course
quests.description: Drive through the first red ring to begin the course. This one"s got a tricky jump to it.  [Go]
quests.completionMessage: Congratulations!  You"ve reached "Blue Course".  At the end of this course is a single blue ring.  Reach this ring before the timer runs out to complete this course. [More]

quests.title: Blue Course
quests.description: Drive through the first blue ring to begin the course. Can you find the shortest route?  [Go]
quests.completionMessage: You have successfully completed all four courses!    You are now ready to challenge the next track! Prepare for the next Track! [Next]

quests.title: Track Complete
quests.description: "You must be a citizen to advance to the next level."
quests.completionMessage: "Welcome to the next level!"

quests.title: Intro
quests.completionMessage: "Hello, I am Tinker. I have the relatively unique ability to marry the technology of engineering and magery. Using my latest invention, the Transmorphonizer 9000(tm), which is here to my left. I can upgrade some of the more primitive non-biological range weapons. Currently, the T-9000(tm) can upgrade the Acid Guns used by Humans and the common Blobic Genshock. One more thing... I hate to be a stickler, but you must be able to arm the weapon in order to upgrade it." [More]

quests.title: Prepare The Experimental Upgrade
quests.description: "Bring me six Clegorn Tongues as a normal channel reagent, six Aqua Tofani as a catalyst, and a warp cell to provide a semi-stable warp field,"
quests.completionMessage: "Oh no, you are going to think I"m really dumb, but I forgot an essentiial ingredient. Duh, Plasma. I"m fresh out. Let me think... [More]

quests.title: Oh Yes, almost forgot
quests.description: "Ah yes, I"ve got it... A squidlike creature roaming the lake is a great source of plasma. Bring me the plasma, and while your at it, loot its tentacles for me. They are quite good served Tempura style."
quests.completionMessage: "Mmmm Crition Tentacles. I"ll just take those from you. You can just keep the Plasma with you. You"ll want to have it and your weapon with you when you enter the T-9000(tm).  Now Just step in to the T-9000(tm) to my left and voila! You just may end up with a better weapon than you currenly had... You see I"ve learned recently that there is an uncertainty factor that I cannot eliminate. Anyhow, I"ve already loaded up the machine. So get in... That is unless you are willing to take a risk with the, slightly more volatile, T-9000 Verson 2.0(tm)..." [More]
quests.hint: Retreive Plasma and Tentacles from Crition.

quests.title: Experment Ready
quests.description: "If you are willing to test my latest and greatest invention, Instead of entering the T-9000(tm), you can head over to the Trendor Engineering lab and talk to my assistant Bra"tang. He"s just putting the finishing touches on the new T-9000 v2.0(tm), and may need you to assist. I warn you, it can be risky. Otherwise, you can play it safe and use the old version here, to my left."

quests.title: Hint
quests.completionMessage: "So you, little puny mortal, think you impress the leaders of the grounce race? Ha! You would have to do something truly amazing to do that. You could talk to Sarin-Slayer inside the Black Market caves if you truly want to prove yourself to us."

quests.title: Intro
quests.description: "You"re too weak! Go away!"
quests.completionMessage: "So, you"re the mortal who wishes to prove himself to the Grounce race? Only a few of your kind have attempted this, and most have perished." [More]

quests.title: Proving yourself: Step 1
quests.description: "But, if you want to make an impression, there"s no better place to start than with me. You see, of all the Grounce race, I am different. You see, the only thing I hate more than people like you, is Sarins. I want you to bring me 10 Sarin Hearts to show me that you show no mercy when dealing with their pathetic kind."
quests.completionMessage: "You got them, most impressive. But I am sure your success will not survive my next task for you." [More]

quests.title: Proving Yourself: Surprise
quests.description: "Where was I... WHAT?... NOT AGAIN!... See this is why I hate Sarins. Get rid of it, quick. Don"t let it get away."
quests.completionMessage: "See what I mean. Its like they appear out of thin air. Their meaty too, not like deathbots. The Grounce have a distaste for "meaty" creatures." [More]

quests.title: Proving yourself: Step 2
quests.description: "Now, where was I...Oh yes, you were trying to gain my trust and respect. Well, I suppose you can do one thing for me. Seek out the Sarin who is called Bob. I"ve been told he carries something valuable with him sometimes, come back when you have that item."
quests.completionMessage: "This is good, not a very diffucult task, but I suppose it proves that you really want to do this." [More]
quests.hint: You can find Bob on Moons Rift

quests.title: Proving yourself: Step 3
quests.description: "I have only one final task for you, bring me the remains of the rune lord who has befriended the Sarin race, Skelcy."
quests.completionMessage: "Amazing! You actually got it! Well, this is enough to convince me that you are truly a friend of the Grounce race. But alas, I only carry a little weight in our proud society." [More]
quests.hint: Did I do the Rune Quest?

quests.title: Complete
quests.description: "To further increase your status with our great race, talk to my old friend Hijon-Hacker, in the channels of the Catacombs."

quests.title: Intro
quests.description: "What are you doing here? Go away, puny mortal."
quests.completionMessage: "I see Sarin-Slayer thinks you are worthy of my attention. He has trained differently than I, and doesn"t really understand the primary threat to our species. Among the Grounce, the Godions are a focused race. We believe that to achieve, one must fixate on a specific goal. My goal is to rid this place of those crude, stomping, throwers of rocks, the Hijon race. You can prove your worth to me by accepting a challenge." [More]

quests.title: Proving Yourself Step 1
quests.description: "Okay brave soul, Let us test your mettle. There is a room not far from hear that usually infested with the putrid smelling Rancons. Bring me 5 of their hides as proof of your committment to my cause."
quests.completionMessage: "Not bad, Sarin-Slayer may have been right about you. Tell you what, I"m going to tell you a short story about my first run-in with a Tilidon. You think Rancons are bad, Tilidons are worse." [More]

quests.title: Tilidion Story 1 of 3
quests.completionMessage: "I was engaging in a quest assigned to me by master Hijon-Hunter. I was told that I would be sent to euthanize a crippled Tilidion. Well to make a long bloody story short, I was ambushed by several very healthy Tilidions. Apparently, they had sensed that their kindred was near death, and arrived just before I did. As much as I and my clan have distaste for the Hijon race, we can"t bear to see one suffer. Death in battle is honorable, but a slow lingering death is distasteful." [More]

quests.title: Tilidion Story 2 of 3
quests.completionMessage: "I was mercilessly attacked by the Tilidions, and left for dead. The only reason I am still here today is because of my, now blood brother Sarin-Slayer, Found my tattered body and administered the last of the Sun Elixirs left to him by his teacher, Sarin-Smiter, who was slayed during a Sarin raid in Black Market. Grounce-Lord rest his soul." [More]

quests.title: Tilidion Story 3 of 3
quests.completionMessage: "I have a bone to pick with the Tilidions and I need you to help me right this minute. I"ll take your continued palaver as a Yes." [More]

quests.title: Proving Yourself Step 2
quests.description: "Using a call known only to my clan, I"ve summoned a Tildion for you to battle. Retrieve the stone he carries, and come back to me and I will summon another. When I have enough of these stones, I will be able to pay back Sarin-Slayer my blood debt to him. You should find the Tildion waiting for you in a flooded chamber below this place."
quests.completionMessage: "My heart is lifted, and I"m beginning to believe that you are truly worthy of my approval. I need you to perform one last task to seal the deal." [More]

quests.title: Proving Yourself Step 3
quests.description: "My debt to Sarin-Slayer must be repayed in a tradition specific to our upbringing. The three stones represent the three Tilidions that left me for dead. Two additional stones icons must be included, along with the actual item that was sacrificed to save me. Bring to me a Grey-Stone Rune, a Blue-Stone Rune, and 5 Sun Elixirs to annoint the 5 stones."
quests.completionMessage: "You are a most worthy force in Iia. My gratitude is topped only by my respect for you. If I can manage to escape the Catacombs with my stones, I will be able to finally move on with my life. Otherwise, I"ll still be here awaiting another brave soul to test, to guide, and I hope, to respect." [More]

quests.title: Complete
quests.description: "Go now. Another of my race will be awaiting your arrival. You can find him near a place known as Death Valley. His name is Braun-Butcher."

quests.title: Intro
quests.description: "Ssssh, I"m busy hunting."
quests.completionMessage: "Hi, many don"t appreciate the thrill of the hunt. I understand you"ve met a few of my friends. They speak highly of you, but I"m concerned that you might be deluded by their obsessions. I"m not obsessed, I just know good food when I smell it. Of all the creatures in Iia, the Braun are the most pungeant. Would you let me teach you the fine art of hunting, and preparing Braun in the tradition of my upbringing?" [More]

quests.title: Proving yourself: Step 1
quests.description: "So you do want to prove yourself? The first thing I need you to do is to get me a few good slices of each of the Braun creatures."
quests.completionMessage: "Good work, now we have to prepare these delicious parts for ingestation." [More]

quests.title: Proving yourself: Step 2
quests.description: "What I need from you now, is a Scroll of Flame Missile, and a Scroll of Radius Flame Attack."
quests.completionMessage: "Good, you got them, now I can make our main course."
quests.hint: Where can you find Magic Scrolls?

quests.title: Proving yourself: Step 3
quests.description: "Now, for the dessert. I have something very special planned for this. There is an ancient Grision roaming somewhere in the Firetown caves that drops the most delicious eyes you have ever tasted. Get those for me, and we can finally eat this masterpiece."
quests.completionMessage: "Ah, finally, you got them. Let me just mix all these things together..." [More]
quests.hint: The Grision in the Cave of Ancients

quests.title: Proving yourself: Dinner
quests.completionMessage: "Mmm, this is good. You know the old rogue bloblic called Grez-Orb? You might remember him as an agitator against the frog race." [More]

quests.title: Proving yourself: Fight!
quests.description: "I invited him to this dinner, you didn"t really think I"d settle for a meal consisting solely of Braun? A little dash of $CHARNAME should make this meal perfect!"
quests.completionMessage: "Oh, I"m so sorry! Please don"t kill me!" [More]

quests.title: Complete
quests.description: "Next, you must seek out Cribuant-Carver in the Human City."

quests.title: Intro
quests.description: "GO AWAY!"
quests.completionMessage: "Thank you for sparing the life of old Braun-Butcher. It showed us that you have compassion, even for those who are lesser than the rest of us." [More]

quests.title: Proving yourself: Step 1
quests.description: "My...passion, so to speak, is Cribuants. These wonderfully meaty creatures have a very good taste in valuable gems. I want you to hunt Wispions until you get the Format Gem for me, an ancient gem that was created to remember the great immortal Format C:\, who served us ages ago."
quests.completionMessage: "Ah, you got it! This is a valuable part of the history of IIA to our people. But wait, I am not done with you." [More]
quests.hint: Get the Format Gem from the Wispions

quests.title: Proving yourself: Step 2
quests.description: "I need you to retreive another artifact of great historical importance. The Vinzalf Gem. The Gopes are in possesion of this artifact at the moment, retreive it for me."
quests.completionMessage: "Ah, you got it, great work. There"s just one more favour I need from you." [More]
quests.hint: Get the Vinzalf Gem from the Gopes

quests.title: Proving yourself: Step 3
quests.description: "The last thing I need you to get for me is yet another part of our ancient history. What I need is the fabled Caldris gem that many beleived were lost forever. However, I have found out that the Uatos have this gem in their possesion at the time being. You have to retreive it for me."
quests.completionMessage: "Good work, now, let me just translate the inscriptions on these gems." [More]
quests.hint: Get the Caldris gem from the Uatos

quests.title: Proving yourself: History lession
quests.completionMessage: "Let"s see here...The Grounce were originally created to oppose the bloblics on their home world, Malia. After several fierce battles, the Grounce Elders decided to perform a tactical withdrawal from Malia...They came here and established a community. After a long time, several branches of the Grounce race evolved from the Godions. The violent Clidions were the first branch, followed closely by the capitalistic Kandra. After a long while, and extended exposure to technology, the technology-loving Godions broke away from the rest of the Godions and slowly developed into the proud Rigprion race." [More]

quests.title: Proving yourself: History lession 2
quests.completionMessage: "After a long time of peace, the mortal races invaded IIA, and war broke out again. The Grounce races again formed an alliance, and fought together for a long period of time. After many years of war, the Grounce race, finally facing defeat, split up. Now only a few of the different species remain, and those who are still here cling to the hope of revenge." [More]

quests.title: Proving yourself: History lession 3
quests.completionMessage: "During recent years, relative peace has fallen over the entire Grounce race, they can even be found cooperating with the mortal races. There is also a mention of a bloblic named Site who was trying to gather together an army to defeat the Grounce, once and for all... I wonder if that could be..." [More]

quests.title: Proving yourself: Blob hunt
quests.description: "You must go quickly and investigate this matter. We have had recent reports of a Bloblic called Site trying to cause trouble for us, our last report was that he was planning a strategy in the deepest parts of the Solothic caves. If you go now, you might catch him alone, hurry! And make sure to loot his body too."
quests.completionMessage: "Ah, so our piece remains intact, for now. You have proved yourself as a useful companion." [More]
quests.hint: Kill Site in the Solothic caves

quests.title: Complete
quests.description: "Hmm, he had the gem of an unknown deity on him. We must investigate this matter. You have gained the trust of the Godion species. You must now move on to the Clidions. You can find Clith in the tunnel that leads to FireTown."
quests.hint: Find Clith in the Jouster Maze

quests.title: Intro
quests.description: "Go away, Imposter."
quests.completionMessage: "Fear...  That"s what binds the hands of the Godions. Fear. The fools can"t see the forest for the trees. It"s no wonder they sent you on to us. They aren"t qualified to judge themselves, much less others. Most of the trash, like you, that they send our way end up dead, or worse, left wishing for death," [More]

quests.title: Enlightenment Step 1
quests.description: "I and my kind will open your eyes to the Way. The Way is what we call the path we follow, The Way carries us from the Legacy. Yes, the Way... and the Legacy... First you will learn of the Legacy. To see the Legacy is the first step to knowing it. We need eyes to see. Get me eyes from Pidion, Infant Dilirum, Taldon, Eyemba, Eyezora, Grision, Scout, Kidion, Crid, and lastly the Eyezion."
quests.completionMessage: "Yesss, to see the Legacy is one part of knowing, but one must also feel the Legacy. Clidions, like your race, feel more with their hearts than they do with their hands." [More]

quests.title: Enlightenment Step 2
quests.description: "The power of the Way is derived from the Legacy. It pulses with the ebb and flow of the energy of all living beings. Bring me the hearts of Dark Jouster, Sarin, Mad Kidion, and the ever-so-rarely recovered Kidion Heart. I would suggest starting with the Dark Jouster behind you..."
quests.completionMessage: "There that wasn"t so hard. Let me add those to the others. Yesss, we are almost there. There"s something missing. Oh yes, the Legacy. We can see it, feel it, We must hear it." [More]
quests.hint: Hearts from Dark Jouster, Sarin, Mad Kidion, Kidion

quests.title: Enlightenment Step 3
quests.description: "Bring me the ears from 10 of those misguided Godions that seem to like you so much."
quests.completionMessage: "Exxxxcellent, you see, no matter how you defeat an enemy, to take their eyes, heart, ears from a carcass you need a knife. When you were cutting the organs from these pitiful creatures, did you not feel the power of the Legacy. The Legacy of our ancestors is our affinity for the razor sharp weapons of honor. Melee is an underappreciated skill. When you are done savoring the imagery, I will prepare your path along the Way..." [More]

quests.title: Enlightenment Step 4
quests.description: "I"ve spread a paste made from the items you retrieved on a stone near a naturally heated vent here in the cave floor. The mixture should burn and create a wisp of smoke than when breathed should help to show you the Way....  Uh Oh, I think I added too much of something, quick.... Kill it," [More]
quests.completionMessage: "Why does that always happen? Here, you"ve got my vote. Oh and by the way, thanks for the silver ring you got from the Wartraon, you can have this wonderul key in return. You may need it down the road."

quests.title: Complete
quests.description: "My opinion is my own. You still need to convince others of your worthiness. I suggest starting with Phlim."
quests.hint: Find Phlim in Air Kingdom near Clegorns

quests.title: Intro
quests.description: "I have nothing to say to your kind."
quests.completionMessage: "Don"t tell me... Clith sent you. He is my junior and it is understandable that he ran into a brick wall trying to explain the Way. He barely understands himself. You apparenly understand that melee is more than a choice for us. The Way is really just a set of rules we live our lives by."

quests.title: The four paths of the Way - Patience
quests.description: "Patience will be awarded on this step in your journey. Retreive for me an item taken from my friend Glot while he was traveling along the Eastern shore of the Dark Sea to meet me. I was awating his letter and never received it. The opportunities to retrieve it will be intermittent so you must bide your time, and be prepared to act on a moments notice."
quests.completionMessage: "You have proved that patience is a virtue. And you are most virtuous. Come back when you are ready to continue your travels along the Way."
quests.hint: Await Sarin Raid Near BM Building

quests.title: The four paths of the Way - Persistance
quests.description: "Are you patient, or are you just Lucky. Lets see how lucky you are in this test of persistance. I have placed a small red pin on a creature common in the Air Kingdom. Kill these creatures until you retreive this item."
quests.completionMessage: "You seem persistant enough.You"ve made it this far. But again, luck may be on your side. A further test is necessary. Return when you feel strong enough to take on a test of strength."

quests.title: The four paths of the Way - Serenity
quests.description: "You may be surprised that for many, strength can give an extreme sense of serentity. One of the stronger creatures that inhabit this land guards the outer regions of the Air Kingdom, but you never know where they may pop up... On one of these creatures is an Amulet. Retrieve it now and prove that you can use strength to achieve serenity."
quests.completionMessage: "I knew that you could. I"ve begun to trust in that. But the question is; Can you trust me? We"ll see..." [More]
quests.hint: Hunt Pet Torik for an Amulet

quests.title: The four paths of the Way - Trust
quests.description: "Have a nice flight..."
quests.completionMessage: "I am happy to have earned your trust, friend." [More]

quests.title: Complete
quests.description: "Like I said, the Way is like a path. We know it starts at the Legacy, but where does it take us. Seek Phreg for the answer to that question."

quests.title: Intro
quests.description: "Bah!"
quests.completionMessage: "Finally. you made it. I haven"t got a lot of time. I understand you"ve spoken with a few of my acquaintances. I received a communique earlier from Crib-Carver. He gave you a bit of a history lesson. As you now understand, and by the fact that we"re tallking; Our race is no longer so focused on conflict. The Way leads us from the Legacy, and to the Unhappened, or the future as your race refers to it." [More]

quests.title: Intro2
quests.completionMessage: "Like all beings, along the Way, or in the present as it were, we must learn and change to prepare ourselves for the Unhappened. Come back and speak with me if you agree. But don"t think about too long. Time is of the essence. Change is in the air. I need you to perform a mission." [More]

quests.title: Secret Mission
quests.description: "I need you to find my Master. His name is Clugoth. We don"t have much time. Please do what he says. He can be found in a underground installation on Bloblic Colony. Take the tunnel near the lagoon to reach him. If you don"t make it in time, you"ll have to come back and speak with me again."
quests.completionMessage: "Oh your back... I forgot to send some Waterspore with you. I have a few cases of it here. Oh well. I see by this list that we"ll need to work with the Kandra. They won"t cooperate easily. If they do, it will cost an arm and a leg. Anyhow, you have the Clidion vote of confidence. Don"t lose it." [More]
quests.hint: You have 10 min.to locate Clugoth on Bloblic Colony.

quests.title: Complete
quests.description: "You have the Clidion vote, Seek Knopic in the Four Falls Crypt. He will find someone to help interpret this list."

quests.title: Intro
quests.description: "I asked that you be told to hurry. My contact has left. Apparently you didn"t get the message. Go back to Phreg and see if he"ll arrange to recall my contact."
quests.completionMessage: "Ah, you"ve made it in time. My contact hasn"t even showed up yet." [More]

quests.title: Busy Work
quests.description: "I"ve been holed up here a long time. Please, until my contact arrives, I cannot leave. Would you bring me some food. I really require a good source of Omega 3. Waterspores can be harvested from the rare male Guab Fish. I"m not sure where you find them this time of year. I"ll need a few dozen at least though."
quests.completionMessage: "Ah thanks, just in time too. My contact has just left. Oh and one more thing..." [More]

quests.title: One more thing
quests.description: "I need something to gobble my waterspores out of. Get me a Torik shell as they are just the right size. There, over there.. that Normal channel Torik will have one."
quests.completionMessage: "Thanks, now take this list of components back to Phreg. And don"t listen to his mumbo jumbo about the Unhappened. We need to move on. You are playing a big part in it too. We are preparing a package to deliver to the Rigprions. They are the only Grounce who have a bent towards technology, and we need them right now. The Kandra will have their part in this too." [More]

quests.title: Complete
quests.description: "Hurry, Phreg is awaiting your swift return."

quests.title: Destination
quests.completionMessage: Reached

quests.title: Terminal Velocity
quests.completionMessage: Dum dee dum...

quests.title: Intro
quests.description: "Grrr."
quests.completionMessage: "I was told you"d be coming to speak with me. "$CHARNAME", isn"t it? No matter, you can tell the Clidions that we"re not going to cooperate unless we get something for our trouble. Besides, they won"t tell us WHY the Rigprions need these things. I"ll just be taking that list for now." [More]

quests.title: Pay up 1
quests.description: "Well, all I have for you is information. You appear poorer than Boomtown Tourist. But lets find out how "resourceful" you can be. You see I"m carrying no sword. Bring me a sword. A normal channel (AP) Omsevenier will do just fine. If you can"t afford one, too bad."
quests.completionMessage: "Hmmm, you are quite resourceful. But I need further proof that you are a person of at least some wealth. I plan on opening a small shop to trade my wares. Justic can"t seem to see fit to trade with me. He doesn"t appreciate the art of the haggle. He insists on making me pay the full amount. Here are the credits I have available." [More]

quests.title: PAY UP 2
quests.description: "All you must do is pay the difference. I realize that I"m overly generous for a Kandra, but you only live once. Now go! Get me a Commerce Installation."
quests.completionMessage: "Ok, Ok. I"m convinced. Take the Component List to Kvisich. He"s help you interpret this list so you can gather the items the Rigprions require to do whatever they do." [More]
quests.hint: Buy a Commerce Installation for Knopic

quests.title: Complete
quests.description: "Kvisich can be found nearby."
quests.hint: Find Kvisich in Four Falls Crypt

quests.title: Intro
quests.description: "Get your own pile of bricks."
quests.completionMessage: "I"m watching you. These bricks are mine, all mine. Don"t even think about taking one. Hmm? Oh, Knopic sent you? You have the list?" [More]

quests.title: Do you have the list?
quests.description: "If you don"t have the list, I can"t help you."
quests.completionMessage: "Good, okay let me look this over.... Well I can"t say that I understand the list, You may want to get something to write with." [More]

quests.title: Get this stuff
quests.description: "The list says to get 10 Fuel Cells (from some Sarins), 10 Warp Cells, 1 Ash Rune (see Wa`nuk), and 150k Credits. Be warned, Fuel Cells are very bulky. You may want to make room."
quests.completionMessage: "Ahh yes, You"ve broght what I needed. I was just kidding about the credits. I have more than enough. Especially since I"ve claimed this crumbling pile of Bricks." [More]
quests.hint: Get the supplies and come back to me.

quests.title: Complete
quests.description: "I"ll have these items sent to Rictav. Now go find him as he may require more." [Complete]

quests.title: Intro
quests.description: "Do I know you?"
quests.completionMessage: "Ah, so there you are. I have received the items you gathered to help make the Seismographic Data Analyzer." [More]

quests.title: Item Creation: Part 1
quests.description: "But wait, you are missing some of the most vital components, the gems you need to focus the data streams! First off, get the Dragon Gem. It is said that the lonely BRAG sometimes carries it in it"s mouth when it"s out rolling."
quests.completionMessage: "Ah, so you got it, very good, but there are still a few gems that need to be retrieved for the analyzer to work." [More]
quests.hint: BRAG is near the old Bloblic Outpost

quests.title: Item Creation: Part 2
quests.description: "This time, I need you to retrieve the Mango Gem from the Necrolaz that invade the Air Kingdom from time to time."
quests.completionMessage: "Good work, I should be able to engineer the item after you get me the last gem." [More]
quests.hint: Kill Necrolaz in the Air Kingdom

quests.title: Item Creation: Part 3
quests.description: "The last gem I need you to retreive is the  Roamer Gem, this gem is once in a while found on the corpse of a dead Drakite. This is however not common at all, so you might spend a while trying to get it."
quests.completionMessage: "Great work! Now all I have to do is assemble these items to form the Seismic Data Analyzer." [More]
quests.hint: Hunt Drakites. There is one near Bloblic Colony that is an easy target.

quests.title: Assembling the item
quests.completionMessage: "Now let"s see here...Yes, here we go...There, it"s working, and broadcasting the data. Unfortunately, I can"t receive the data that it is broadcasting, you need a SDA Reader to do that." [More]

quests.title: Complete
quests.description: "You have to seek out Rofftiq about the SDA Reader, you can find him on the highest hill on UOC Penn."
quests.hint: Find Rofftiq on the highest hill on UOC Penn

quests.title: Intro
quests.description: "What are you doing here?"
quests.completionMessage: "Ah, you are here for the SDA Reader then? I have one, but it lacks a power source." [More]

quests.title: The SDA Reader: Part 1
quests.description: "The SDA Reader is powered by the plasma energy found in Wright Plasma. Get 10 Wright Plasma , that should be enough power."
quests.completionMessage: "Good, now let me try this...Yes, it"s working! But wait..." [More]

quests.title: The SDA Reader: Part 2
quests.description: "This can"t be right, it"s reporting that a drastic change in the geology is imminent! I need you to go to two of our main seismic data storages and confirm this data."
quests.completionMessage: "Dear lord, the data is accurate. You will have to take this information to the Grounce Lord." [More]
quests.hint: Mining Cave and the top of a hill on the Human Island

quests.title: Complete
quests.description: "You can interact with him through one of the cracks in the Jouster Maze tunnel. Sometimes he can be away for long periods of time. so check back."

quests.title: Intro
quests.completionMessage: "How dare you disturb me, fragile being?" [More]

quests.title: Grounce Lord
quests.completionMessage: "You bring news of great importance? Nothing in this world can endanger the Grounce race, begone, or I will unleash my anger upon you." [More]

quests.title: Fight!
quests.description: "You have wasted enough of my time, the dawn of your doom is upon us."
quests.completionMessage: "What? You defeated my guard? Then I shall endure your senseless ramblings." [More]

quests.title: Explanation
quests.completionMessage: "You can"t be serious, a major shift in the geology of IIA? That isn"t possible! Let me confer with Rofftiq..." --You sense incomprehensable whispers in the back of your head--

quests.title: Explanation 2
quests.completionMessage: "He has confirmed your story... The whole Grounce race must prepare for this event. Thank you for aiding us in this way, you have spared innumerable lives." [More]

quests.title: Reward
quests.completionMessage: "Take this key, it will open a chest containing one of the lost melee weapons for your race." [More]

quests.title: Complete
quests.description: "Look for the chests in your home town in IIA."
quests.hint: Search the old habitat of your people for the chest

quests.completionMessage: "Have you gained the trust of the Grounce race? If you have, then there is a human female who stops by this island from time to time who will want to see you."

quests.title: (AP) Rare melee
quests.description: "I can provide you with an enhanced Sword of Crom that the Godions have entrusted me, if you assist me with a few simple tasks. Get these items for me. You can get the egg from the most powerful Torik in the Air Kingdom. A complete list of items can be found by looking deeply into your quest journal."

You can get the egg from the most powerful Torik in the Air Kingdom. A complete list of items can be found by looking deeply into your quest journal."
